rationale: C14 plausibly supplied a material drafting template because it uses the same national-park enlargement machinery: statutory authorization to add described lands, an operative proclamation adding them to the park, a provision making nonfederal lands part of the park upon United States acquisition of title, and application of the National Park Service organic act together with other park laws and regulations. C06 and C24 contain closely related acquisition-upon-title language, but concern national monuments under different statutory authority.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do proclaim that the lands hereinafter described are hereby added to the Rocky Mountain National Park
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the following-described lands within the boundaries of the Olympic National Forest are hereby added to and reserved as a part of the Olympic national Park
shared_material.explanation: Both operative provisions enlarge a named national park by proclamation and immediately introduce formal land descriptions.

shared_material.child_excerpt: shall, upon acquisition of title thereto by the United States, become subject to
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the lands within such areas which are not now owned by the United States shall become a part of such park upon acquisition of title thereto by the United States
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same contingent-acquisition mechanism for land not yet federally owned.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the act entitled "An Act to establish a National Park Service, and for other purposes," approved August 25, 1916 ... and all acts supplementary thereto and amendatory thereof, and all other laws and rules and regulations applicable to such park
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the act entitled "An act to establish a national Park Service, and for other purposes", approved August 25, 1916 ... and acts supplementary thereto or amendatory thereof, and to all other laws, rules, and regulations applicable to the said park
shared_material.explanation: This is closely parallel language specifying the governing legal regime for lands added to a national park.
